limits: Only three tissues, so one is held out per split.
Removing a tissue also removes its one-hot column, which is part of the design.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

the_qualifier_is_wrong.predicted: pathway positive when the tissue is known and not positive when the tissue is held out
the_qualifier_is_wrong.conclusion: the pathway increment is present, and if anything larger, when the tissue has never been seen. The qualifier inferred from R119 was wrong.

why_R119_was_wrong.R119_design: it used the sparse boolean Synergy flag with k equal to 20 on subsamples, and the combo arm included the tissue block
two_problems: the sparse criterion has no resolution: R122 measured identity at 1.30 percent against a minimum detectable effect of 1.02 pp
the combo arm carried the tissue block, whose columns are dead under tissue holdout, so the reversal was about the dead block plus an unresolvable criterion, not about transfer
why_R119_was_wrong.consequence: C90 should be retracted. The 'tissue must be in distribution' qualifier is wrong and must be removed from the condition statement.

a_clean_internal_control.observation: in the held-tissue pool the tissue block delivers exactly +0.0000 [-0.0104, +0.0102]
a_clean_internal_control.why_it_matters: a block whose columns never appear in training contributes nothing, and the design recovers that exactly. So the apparatus can detect a dead block, and the pathway block is not dead.
a_clean_internal_control.reading: the pathway gain in the same pool is +8.12 pp, so the two blocks are cleanly separated

controls_that_behave.random_block: never significant in any pool or round
controls_that_behave.tissue_block_under_holdout: exactly zero, as it must be

the_stable_picture.statement: when both drugs are unseen, the pathway annotation adds 4.7 to 8.6 pp, and this holds whether the cell is seen, unseen, or from an unseen tissue
